citation.title: Robust Estimation of a Location Parameter
citation.volume: not printed in the supplied pages (bibliographic records give 35)
citation.doi_or_arxiv: not printed in the supplied PDF; verify before use

topic: Minimax asymptotic-variance M-estimation of location under epsilon-contaminated normal models; Huber rho/psi; scale estimation
own_question: Which translation-invariant estimators minimize the worst-case asymptotic variance when a fraction epsilon of observations are gross errors?
actual_method_and_evidence: The paper is asymptotic theory with saddlepoint proofs. It shows that, under symmetric contamination, a quadratic-then-linear rho is minimax (Sections 5-6). Table I tabulates analytic variance bounds. Monte Carlo is mentioned only as an exploratory check of iteration and convergence. There is no time series and no fusion content.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: A loss that is quadratic near zero and linear in the tails bounds the influence of gross errors. Under symmetric epsilon-contamination, it minimizes worst-case asymptotic variance.
claim_checks.qualification: The result is asymptotic, for i.i.d. location estimation with known epsilon and symmetric contamination. Asymmetric contamination introduces bias (Sec. 7).

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Not applicable: the source treats i.i.d. samples with no timing.
validation_if_relevant: Not applicable: the source is analytic, with no data split.
